record.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
record.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare DREAM_EATER (catalog passive NONE). The strategy is shared; differences are star count and stats. The ability has two mutually exclusive branches depending on whether ANY enemy on the board is asleep when it is cast.
record.summary: Two branches, chosen by scanning the whole board for the first enemy that is asleep. (1) A sleeping enemy exists: the caster moves to a nearest empty neighbour cell of that sleeper if one is free, then deals SPECIAL damage (requested 45 / 90 / 150 / 250 by stars) to that sleeper - not necessarily the cast target - and requests a heal of 1 x the takenDamage that call returned (apBoost 0, crit false). takenDamage is the returned figure (shield part, capped HP part, zero for blocked / dead / Shiny Charm, Fossil extension, cover ally's result), not universally the HP lost. handleHeal is called in this order (core-mechanics.md section J2): the wound branch first - a wounded recipient gets no HP, but with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by its player the same call requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw requested heal), recipient, apBoost, crit) with the recipient as the shield's caster, which the entity addShield (Big Eater Belt) turns into the final shield; then the guard hp > 0 && !status.protect (an unwounded Protected recipient gets nothing; Rune Protect alone does not block); then the modifiers (AP, crit, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, ZENITH x1.2), Math.round and the cap at missing HP; the post-modifier overheal on a Grass-synergy recipient requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal), which also raises current HP. 'No direct HP healing' therefore does not mean 'no shield or max-HP / current-HP effect'. Requested amount, handleHeal's returned healReceived / overheal and the final stored hp / maxHP / shield are three different things. (2) No enemy is asleep: the code builds targetThatCanSleep = the first of [cast target, then every enemy in board order] that has no Rune Protect, is not skydiving, lacks IMMUNITY_SLEEP and has ccCooldown <= 0. If one is found, sleep is attempted on the ORIGINAL CAST TARGET, not on the enemy that was found, for round([3000, 4000, 5000, 6000][stars - 1] x (1 + AP/100)) ms through triggerSleep, whose own guards (already asleep, Rune Protect, skydiving, IMMUNITY_SLEEP, ccCooldown) can refuse it; and the strategy then assigns pokemon.pp = maxPP directly, whether or not the original target accepted the sleep. If nobody qualifies nothing happens. PP: the base class cost is max(0, pp - maxPP), so the damage branch RETAINS the excess (150 PP with maxPP 100 ends at 50, never 'zero'); the sleep branch overwrites PP with maxPP (100 PP stays 100, 150 PP becomes 100), which is not a universal refund of the cost and does not promise an instant cast (the cast gate and canCast still apply). Requested numbers: DROWZEE (1 star) 45 damage / 3000 ms; HYPNO (2 stars) 90 damage / 4000 ms.

targeting.who: branch 1: the first sleeping enemy found scanning the board by rows (y, then x), anywhere on the board; branch 2: the cast target passed to the strategy (the sleep is requested on it), after a candidate check that includes other enemies
targeting.note: requiresTarget is the base default true; target selection before the cast was not read.

geometry.shape: single target; branch 1 also relocates the caster
geometry.movement: caster swaps into a random one of the nearest empty cells within Manhattan distance 1 of the sleeper; no move if none is free (the damage still happens)

effects.scaling: requested raw amount; AP: x (1 + caster AP/100) (apBoost explicitly true); the cast's crit factor only if the cast crit (canCritByDefault false, needs ABILITY_CRIT)
effects.resolution: applied change: blocked by protect / skydiving / magicBounce on the sleeper (takenDamage 0, so no heal); otherwise handleDamage divides by (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF), ceil, min 1, then shield, Shiny Charm, Fossil and Cover Band branches fix takenDamage (rounded). The sleep reduction is settled: PokemonState.handleDamage calls pokemon.onDamageReceived only when takenDamage > 0 and the recipient survives (hp > 0) (pokemon-state.ts:734-743), and onDamageReceived subtracts 300 from a positive sleepCooldown (pokemon-entity.ts:1211-1214), once per such damage instance. It is not called for blocked (protect / skydiving / magic bounce, takenDamage 0), dead or lethal-hit recipients or when Shiny Charm zeroes takenDamage; with a Cover Band redirect the original target is not called (the cover ally's own handleDamage is, for the cover ally); a shield that absorbs everything still counts (takenDamage > 0). The subtraction does not clear the sleep flag: sleepCooldown can go negative while sleep stays true until updateSleep runs in the status update (probe: 200 -> -100, flag still true, then false with ccCooldown 1500).

effects.scaling: 1 x takenDamage returned by handleSpecialDamage; apBoost 0 and crit false are passed, so neither AP nor crit scales it
effects.resolution: requested = 1 x the returned takenDamage (0 requests 0). handleHeal is called in this order (core-mechanics.md section J2): the wound branch first - a wounded recipient gets no HP, but with BLOODMOON weather and a Blood Stone owned by its player the same call requests addShield(round(0.3 x stones x the raw requested heal), recipient, apBoost, crit) with the recipient as the shield's caster, which the entity addShield (Big Eater Belt) turns into the final shield; then the guard hp > 0 && !status.protect (an unwounded Protected recipient gets nothing; Rune Protect alone does not block); then the modifiers (AP, crit, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, ZENITH x1.2), Math.round and the cap at missing HP; the post-modifier overheal on a Grass-synergy recipient requests addMaxHP(0.4 x overheal), which also raises current HP. 'No direct HP healing' therefore does not mean 'no shield or max-HP / current-HP effect'. Requested amount, handleHeal's returned healReceived / overheal and the final stored hp / maxHP / shield are three different things.

effects.scaling: duration = round(base x (1 + caster AP/100)) computed in the strategy (not through an apBoost parameter); no crit scaling
effects.resolution: applied duration: triggerSleep on the cast target then applies, in order, weather (NIGHT x1.3, ZENITH x0.7), enraged /2, then SWIFT_SWIM x0.7 (else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL or SURGE_SURFER x0.3), then Odd Keystone x(1 - 0.1 x count held by the target's player), rounded. It is skipped if the target already sleeps, has Rune Protect, is skydiving, has IMMUNITY_SLEEP or has ccCooldown above 0 (1500 ms after a sleep ends). A Chesto Berry on the target is eaten when sleep starts. Each damage instance that reaches onDamageReceived (positive takenDamage on a surviving recipient, effects[0]) shortens a positive sleepCooldown by 300 ms without clearing the sleep flag.

pokemon.pp = maxPP is assigned whenever a candidate that can sleep was found, whether or not triggerSleep then accepted the sleep on the cast target. After the base cost max(0, pp - maxPP) this OVERWRITES the PP: 100 stays 100, 150 becomes 100 (the retained excess is lost). It is not a refund of the cost in general and does not promise an instant cast.

statusEffects.applicationOrder: after the candidate search; PP then assigned maxPP directly (whether or not the sleep was accepted)
statusEffects.guards: triggerSleep: not already asleep, not Rune Protect, not skydiving, not IMMUNITY_SLEEP, ccCooldown <= 0
statusEffects.combatEffect: a sleeping unit cannot move or act except with the COMATOSE passive (canMove / state checks); sleep ends when the cooldown runs out and gives 1500 ms of crowd-control immunity

starBehavior.note: both tables are indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 3- and 4-star values (150/250 damage, 5000/6000 ms) are declared in the tables but unused by the two bound baseline classes. maxPP 100 and range 2 for both.

record.positionalConditions: Branch 1 ignores range and the cast target: it uses the first sleeping enemy anywhere on the board in row-major order and teleports (swaps) the caster next to it when a free orthogonal neighbour exists. Branch 2 works on the cast target.
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state. Branch 2 sets PP to maxPP, so the next cast is possible as soon as the cast gate is met again (canCast and a target still apply) and, if the target is then asleep, takes branch 1. Branch 1 keeps the excess PP above the base cost (150 PP with maxPP 100 ends at 50), it does not zero it.
record.rawVsResolved: Requested (raw): 45 / 90 damage, 3000 / 4000 ms sleep, heal 1 x takenDamage. Applied: damage x (1 + AP/100) [x crit], / (1 + 0.05 x SPE_DEF) ceil min 1, shield accounting (takenDamage is shield part + HP part, 0 if blocked or Shiny Charm, + Fossil addition, or the cover ally's result); heal passes the handleHeal modifiers and the missing-HP cap; sleep duration x (1 + AP/100) then weather, enraged, duration reductions and the triggerSleep guards (the sleep can be refused while the PP assignment still happens). The heal request (1 x returned takenDamage), handleHeal's returned healReceived / overheal and the final stored values are separate, as are the sleep duration requested (3000 / 4000 x (1 + AP/100)), the duration triggerSleep applies and the sleepCooldown after later 300 ms reductions.
dependsOnUnverifiedGenericCombat: Final damage after handleDamage's later modifiers (items, damage-reduction effects, resurrection, field multipliers) - only SPE_DEF division, ceil/min 1 and the takenDamage branches were located
When the cast fires in a real fight (PP gain, targeting before the cast, silence) - only the pp >= maxPP && canCast gate was read
Crit resolution: only the ABILITY_CRIT / canCritByDefault gate and the damage-side multiplier were read
How a sleeping unit is treated by targeting and attack states beyond the canMove / canCast checks (the other sleep sites in attacking-state / movement were only listed, not read)
unresolved: The source reads as if the sleep is meant for targetThatCanSleep but is applied to the cast target; this record states what the code does (executed: the original target with Rune Protect refuses the sleep while another enemy qualified and PP became maxPP) and does not know the intent

Settled on import: the single caller of onDamageReceived is pokemon-state.ts:734-743 (positive takenDamage on a surviving recipient), so SPECIAL ability damage reduces sleep by 300 ms whenever that condition holds (blocked, dead, lethal, Shiny-Charm-zeroed and Cover-Band-redirected original targets excluded); other damage sources that reach handleDamage follow the same rule, other writers of sleepCooldown were not enumerated
Resurrection paths other than the cited branches and other death-cancelling effects on the sleeper were not enumerated
Whether any other item or synergy effect changes DREAM_EATER beyond what is listed

Both units have passive NONE; no routing uncertainty in the queue record. Evidence: source reading, mechanical checks and executed probes. The pinned helper text (handleDamage, handleSpecialDamage, handleHeal, triggerSleep, updateSleep and the sleep-reduction lines of onDamageReceived) and the real DreamEaterStrategy strategy text were run against stand-in units, boards and call targets (probes/pinned-helper-probe.mjs, sections TAKEN_DAMAGE, SHARED_HELPERS and IMPORT_RECHECK_2); the whole ability in a real fight, targeting and timing before the cast, and full battles were NOT executed, and nothing was observed in a live game.
